title: Drop VAT on the full fare of the largest taxi apps
noun: dropping VAT on the full fare of the largest taxi apps
headline: Drop taxi app VAT. Costs £0.4bn in 2029-30.
description: From January 2028 private hire operators with fares over £50 million a year pay VAT on the whole fare, not just their commission. Switch this on to drop it.

baselinePolicy.text: Larger private hire operators are liable for VAT on the full fare from 2 January 2028 (Table 6.1 line 59).

source.quote: so VAT is charged on the full fare rather than, in the case of agency operators outside London, only the operator’s commission

alreadyIncludes: Larger private hire operators are liable for VAT on the full fare from 2 January 2028 (Table 6.1 line 59).

lines.title: Private Hire Vehicle Operators: Deem larger operators with annual fare turnover over £50 million liable for VAT on the full value of their fares from 2 January 2028

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
